Federal Labor has announced a feasibility study into building a new fuel refinery in WA – a first step towards restoring Australia’s lost refining capacity.
 
They must back up this announcement with a long-term commitment to supporting new investment and job creation in the industry. We need to boost local fuel holdings and refining to meet the moment, while also realising our huge potential in alternative fuels in the longer term.
 
The government has done well to secure emergency fuel import deals in the wake of the Iran-Israel-US war. But relying on a 'friends and allies' fuel security model is a wager, not a strategy.

On Day 2 of the 50th ALP National Conference, AWU Assistant National Secretary Chris Donovan backed reforms to improve jobs, skills, and opportunities for Australians. 

While the Federal Labor government passed Same Job Same Pay laws, employers are using a new loophole to pay some workers less, by misclassifying them as 'trainees'.

That's why we're supporting an amendment to make it absolutely clear to employers - two workers doing the same job, at the same site, must be paid the same.

An incredible 140 years stronger together. 

The AWU recently celebrated our 140th birthday at original site of the Eureka Stockade in Ballarat, a place where our mighty union has gathered to mark 50, 100, and 120 years. 

From the shearing sheds of 1886 to industries across Australia today, our fight remains the same - better wages and conditions, safer workplaces, and secure jobs. 

Thank you to every member from every generation who has kept this union strong.

On Day 1 of the 50th ALP National Conference, our National Secretary Paul Farrow backed Labor's industrial plan to build an economy that serves working people. 

Our gas belongs to us, but instead is being used to supercharge the profits of multinational gas exporters. That's why the AWU is calling on the Labor government to finalise a gas reservation that is fair for workers and the industries that power the nation.

Australian gas must benefit Australian people and Australian industry!

On this day in 1907, the AWU made history by securing Australia's first-ever Federal Industrial Award! 

The Pastoral Workers’ Award increased wages by 20% and set 48-hour working weeks for shearers across the country, with work to stop at midday Saturday. 

The AWU President at the time, William Spence wrote in The Worker: “It only remains now for the members of The Australian Workers’ Union to remain active and true to their principles... to secure still more improvement in many other directions.” 

It stands true to this day. We now cover workers in 78 Industrial Awards across Australia, securing better wages and conditions, improved safety standards, and secure jobs for our members!

AWU WA Branch Secretary Brad Gandy and VIC Branch Secretary Ronnie Hayden travelled to Wales this week representing the Australian Workers’ Union at Community’s 2026 Biennial Delegate Conference.

The conference theme - Strong Union, Strong Future - could not be more relevant.

Across industries and across borders, workers are facing many of the same challenges of rising living costs, insecure work, changing industries, new technology, and overall pressure on wages and conditions.

A key message from the conference is that unions must continue more than ever to organise, grow and empower members at the workplace.

The conference heard first hand from members and delegates regarding the importance of building a strong union by standing together, speaking up and organising on the ground.

Brad and Ronnie met with union leaders, delegates and international representatives to share ideas covering campaigning, workplace organising, leadership and the next generation of union activists.

While our unions may operate in different countries our purpose is the same, giving working people a strong collective voice and delivering better wages, safer workplaces, secure jobs and respect at work.

The lesson from the conference is clear:

When workers are organised, informed and united, we have the power to shape that future, rather than simply having it imposed on us.

Strong unions. Strong workplaces. Strong communities. Strong future.

Happy birthday to prime minister and proud AWU member Gough Whitlam! 🎂

Gough was prime minister of Australia between 1972 and 1975. The brief but revolutionary Whitlam Government secured universal healthcare, free university education, and equal pay, built nation-building freeway and sewerage programs, and abolished the White Australia policy. 

Gough was also a staunch advocate for workers and proud long-term member of the AWU NSW Branch. He passed away in 2014, at the age of 98.

The federal government is currently working through the nuts and bolts of its coming gas reservation, and the AWU has a strong message for gas exporters.

The only way a reservation works is if it really does apply to the big players and treats everyone equally. Any framework that doles out unfair carve-outs will fail. One set of rules needs to apply firmly and its needs to apply to all.

If you want to extract Australia's gas, you must set aside a portion for Australians. No dodgy leave passes, no exceptions!

A Cleanaway worker was left with permanent vision loss after toxic chemical exposure on the job - and the company failed to even report the incident. 

Eight workers have died at Cleanaway in just four years. Their contempt for workers' safety and deplorable record must be investigated. 

Comcare needs to do its job, throw the book at Cleanaway and prosecute them for their failure to keep their workers' safe.

This week, the AWU said farewell to our National Trainer Chris, who is enjoying a very well-earned retirement! 

Chris has trained hundreds of HSRs and delegates across Australia in his five years with the union. 

Thank you, Chris, on behalf of every AWU member who has made their workplace safer and stronger. You will be dearly missed at every AWU office, and we wish you all the best in your retirement.

Payday Super is officially here! 🎉

From now on, your super contributions must be paid into your nominated super fund at the same time as your salary or wages. 

This means that workers will see more gains from their super, as you'll start accumulating interest on your payments faster! 

Make sure you check your super fund seven business days after your wages come in, to make sure you're getting paid - don't rely on payslips alone.
